_comment: Hand-written rows for docs/inventory/userland.tsv: the base user-space commands, daemons and libraries of one release, keyed by install path. Each entry gives the IDB product and subsystem (from the installation media index), a type (daemon, command, library, kernel module, driver tool), the interfaces the binary touches (ioctls, syssgi and sysmp calls, device nodes, sockets, state files), a role in plain words, a grade (established: read in full in the binary at an address; inferred: reasoned from imports, strings and the name; unknown) and a citation naming the strings and imports the reading rests on. Status is located until a routine has been read in full and the role is confirmed; understood needs a grade, a role and a citation specific to the item. The generator reads only these keys and the root/ copies; it takes no role text from anywhere else.

sbin/hinv.interfaces: syssgi and sysmp system calls; the hardware inventory table through scaninvent; the /hw device tree walked with nftw; filename_to_devname and dev_to_devname for device names. Device names in its strings: /hw/gm%d, /hw/net/%s%d, /hw/net/ef%d.
sbin/hinv.role: Prints the hardware inventory of the running machine (processors, memory, boards, adapters and their revisions), from the inventory table and the device tree. Its usage line gives the filters: -v, -m, -s, -c class, -t type, -d device, -u unit and -a file.
sbin/hinv.citation: 6.5.30 sbin/hinv: usage line, inventory and board format strings, and dynamic imports scaninvent, sysmp, syssgi, nftw

sbin/ioconfig.interfaces: ioctl on device vertices under /hw (the strings name /hw/scsi_ctlr, /hw/input*, /hw/xvm, /hw/hw and /hw/.invent); nftw and fnmatch over the device tree; syssgi; chmod and chown; the config files /var/sysgen/ioconfig and /etc/ioconfig.conf; /etc/ioperms.
sbin/ioconfig.role: Applies the ioconfig rule file to the device tree at boot. Each rule gives a class, type, state, case, device-name suffix and pattern, a start number and an ioctl code; the command matches device vertices under /hw against the rules, issues the rule's ioctl to each match, and sets names and permissions. Its error text quotes the rule layout (class type state case suffix pattern start_num ioctl).
sbin/ioconfig.citation: 6.5.30 sbin/ioconfig: rule-format error string, dat:suffix/pattern/start_num/ioctl debug string, /hw and /etc path strings, dynamic imports ioctl, nftw, fnmatch, syssgi, chmod, chown

usr/sbin/numastatd.interfaces: ioctl on the router monitor node and on the L1 controller node found under /hw/module (strings: SNDRV_ACQUIRE_ROUTERINFO and SNDRV_GET_ELSC_VERSION); per-process records under /proc/pinfo; schedctl (RENICE) through cap_acquire and cap_surrender; popen of ls over /hw/module/*/router/mon, /hw/module/*/L1/controller and /hw/module/*/slot/r*/ paths; syssgi; syslog.
usr/sbin/numastatd.role: A single-instance NUMA monitoring daemon for IP27 and IP35 machines. It enumerates routers and L1 controllers from the hardware graph, checks the controller firmware version, reads the router information and per-process records, and adjusts scheduling priority (-n nice value, -w weightless). The per-platform routine names ip27init, ip27setup, ip27acquire, ip27terminate and the ip35 set show the two machine variants it selects between.
usr/sbin/numastatd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/sbin/numastatd: option and status strings (usage, RENICE, weightless), the /hw path strings, the ip27 and ip35 routine names, dynamic imports ioctl, schedctl, popen, syssgi, cap_acquire

usr/etc/mmscd.interfaces: serial console device /dev/console by default, or the device named by -c (MMSC console) and -f (MMSC non-console); ioctl on /dev/console and the controller nodes /hw/machdep/mmsc_control and /hw/machdep/ffsc_control; module nodes /hw/module/%u/slot/n%u/node and /hw/nodenum; sysmp and schedctl; syslog.
usr/etc/mmscd.role: Serial-link daemon for the machine's module management controller (MMSC). It opens the controller serial line at the baud given by -b (-u sets a frequency; its meaning is not read), sends the command set (ping, init, graph start, label, data and end) and collects the replies. Its command names are the only description of the graph commands; their purpose is inferred from the names.
usr/etc/mmscd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/mmscd: usage text (-c, -f, -b, -u), mmsc_* and cmd_* routine names, /hw/machdep and /hw/module path strings, dynamic imports ioctl, sysmp, schedctl, select, read, write

usr/etc/mediad.interfaces: SCSI device nodes /dev/scsi/sc%ud%ul%u and /dev/scsi/%s; floppy nodes /dev/pfd/pfd.2dd and /dev/pfd/pfd.2hd; /etc/config/mediad.config; /etc/mtab and the mount table (getmntent, setmntent); the mount and umount programs through execv; a UNIX socket a UNIX socket under /tmp; RPC registration with pmap_set and pmap_unset over sockets; the file-access monitor (FAMNextEvent); /etc/fsd.auto.
usr/etc/mediad.role: Removable-media manager. It mounts and dismounts removable volumes (CD, floppy and other SCSI media) by the rules in /etc/config/mediad.config, publishes volume and mount state to clients over RPC, and answers showmount-style queries through a compatibility server.
usr/etc/mediad.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/mediad: device, config and socket path strings, C++ class names (Config, Volume, DeviceMonitor, MonitorClient, CompatServer), dynamic imports pmap_set, getmntent, execv, FAMNextEvent

usr/etc/eventmond.interfaces: UNIX socket /tmp/s.eventmond; TCP listen, accept, bind and connect; state files /var/emgr/subscr.eventmond and /var/emgr/tasks.eventmond; dlopen, dlsym and dlclose for task libraries; ftok; syslog.
usr/etc/eventmond.role: Event manager daemon. It accepts events from local and forwarded sources, matches them against subscriptions, forwards them to subscriber hosts, and runs loadable event tasks (LoadTask, TaskStart, TaskStop, TaskList). Its routine names (PassEventToSubscriber, emgrForwardEvent, emgrSendEvent) describe the flow.
usr/etc/eventmond.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/eventmond: state-file and socket path strings, emgr* and emgrcmd_* routine names, dynamic imports dlopen, dlsym, listen, accept, ftok

usr/sbin/sysmon.interfaces: X11 event and widget calls (XtAddEventHandler, the X event-send call); the ViewKit widget classes; the file-access monitor (FAMNextEvent); the notifier configuration /usr/lib/sysmon/notifier.config; the printer spool and line-printer routines (/var/spool/lp, /etc/printcap, lpr and lpq names) in its imports and strings; /var/adm/SYSLOG.
usr/sbin/sysmon.role: Graphical system monitor front end (the Sysmon window and its help). The same program name is also installed from a second product, built for a graphics-board variant; that copy is a separate binary under the same path and is not covered by this row.
usr/sbin/sysmon.citation: 6.5.30 usr/sbin/sysmon: Sysmon and SysmonVersion strings, notifier.config path, X toolkit and ViewKit imports, spool path strings

usr/sbin/l1cmd.interfaces: socket, connect, sendto, recvfrom and gethostbyname for the network path to an L2 controller; serial lines through termios (tcsetattr) for a direct connection; the L1 controller node pattern /hw/module/*c*/L1/controller; getpass for the L2 password; the temporary file /usr/tmp/UNIX_%04x.
usr/sbin/l1cmd.role: Command-line client for the L1 controller of one module (the module management controller). It reaches the L1 directly over a serial line, or through an L2 controller over the network, and sends L1 command packets. Its options (--l2, --sysname, --ssn, --sc, --scdev, --dev, --serial, --interface, --pw, --irtr) select the route. It shares its routine set with the L2 client.
usr/sbin/l1cmd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/sbin/l1cmd: usage and option strings, sn1SC* and L1Direct* routine names, /hw/module L1 controller pattern, dynamic imports connect, sendto and __new_tcsetattr

usr/sbin/l2cmd.interfaces: network sockets to an L2 controller (--l2 host, --interface, --ssn, --sysname); the serial path (--serial, --dev, --scdev); the password prompt; the helper /stand/sysco/bin/l2find named in its error text.
usr/sbin/l2cmd.role: Command-line client for the L2 controller, the rack-level system controller. It finds an L2 by host name, system name or serial number (or by discovery on the L2 network), authenticates with a password, and sends commands. The same routine set as the L1 client (sn1SC* and L1Direct*) implies the same packet protocol.
usr/sbin/l2cmd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/sbin/l2cmd: usage and error strings (--l2, --sysname, --ssn, l2find path), sn1SCDiscoverL2 and sn1SCFindL2 routine names
usr/sbin/l2cmd.limits: The installed file is 848 bytes shorter than its own section header table requires (the table ends past end of file, at offset 446168 + 1560 against 446880 bytes). Program headers read cleanly, so the loadable segments and the string table in them are intact. Section names and the dynamic symbol list are unreadable, so the import count is recorded as unreadable.

usr/etc/nfsd.interfaces: the nfssvc library call, which enters the kernel NFS server; ioctl; /dev/tty.
usr/etc/nfsd.role: NFS server daemon. It starts the kernel NFS server through nfssvc, passing it the server's socket. Its command-line options were not read.
usr/etc/nfsd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/nfsd: dynamic imports nfssvc and ioctl, /dev/tty string

usr/etc/rpc.mountd.interfaces: the mount protocol XDR routines (xdr_mountres3, xdr_fhstatus, xdr_exports, xdr_mountlist); the export table /etc/xtab and the mount record /etc/rmtab; the port range file /etc/rpcports; svc_register for the mount service; ioctl; fork and a rendezvous pipe to worker processes.
usr/etc/rpc.mountd.role: MOUNT protocol server for NFS clients. It checks each mount request against the export table in /etc/xtab, records the active mounts in /etc/rmtab, and runs requests in worker processes.
usr/etc/rpc.mountd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.mountd: /etc/xtab and /etc/rmtab and /etc/rpcports strings, xdr_mountres3 and xdr_exports names, worker and rendezvous-pipe messages, dynamic imports svc_register and ioctl

usr/etc/rpc.lockd.interfaces: the nfssvc library call, which enters the kernel NFS server; a trusted-networking check on the lock socket; the usage line gives the options -l, -g and a grace period with server names.
usr/etc/rpc.lockd.role: Network lock manager (NLM) for NFS. It activates the NLM program, binds the lock socket, and handles lock requests during a grace period after restart.
usr/etc/rpc.lockd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.lockd: usage line (-l -g grace_period servers), 'Unable to activate NLM program' and 'Cannot enable trusted networking' strings, dynamic imports nfssvc and ioctl

usr/etc/rpc.statd.interfaces: the state directory /var/statmon, created and renamed by the daemon; the status monitor calls SM_MON, SM_UNMON and SM_UNMON_ALL, decoded from RPC; svc_run; the usage line options -D, -L, -d debug level, -i delta and -I maximum; HA directory names in its strings.
usr/etc/rpc.statd.role: Network status monitor. It keeps a record of the hosts that hold locks, in /var/statmon, and reports their status changes to the lock manager so that locks can be recovered after a crash or reboot.
usr/etc/rpc.statd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.statd: SM_MON, SM_UNMON and SM_UNMON_ALL decode strings, /var/statmon and the usage line, dynamic imports svc_run and the RPC control call

usr/etc/automount.interfaces: the mount table /etc/mtab; a temporary mount point under /tmp; mount, umount, nfsmount and nfsunmount; pingmount and callrpc to test servers; xdr_exports and xdr_attrstat for replies; ioctl; svc_register for its own service.
usr/etc/automount.role: Automounter. It mounts NFS exports on first access under its mount points and unmounts them after an idle timeout. Its strings name the timeout, the no-mount list and the already-mounted case.
usr/etc/automount.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/automount: the timeout, no-mount-list and already-mounted messages, do_mount, do_unmount and pingmount names, dynamic imports callrpc, ioctl, svc_register

usr/etc/exportfs.interfaces: reads /etc/exports and /etc/nfssec.conf; writes the export table /etc/xtab; getmountid; the superuser check on export and unexport.
usr/etc/exportfs.role: Exports or unexports directories for NFS. It reads the export list, then adds or removes entries in /etc/xtab. Its usage line gives -a (all), -i (ignore the exports file), -u (unexport), -v, -t, -f, -R and -o options.
usr/etc/exportfs.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/exportfs: usage line, /etc/exports, /etc/xtab and /etc/nfssec.conf strings, 'must be superuser' message, getmountid name

usr/etc/rpc.rstatd.interfaces: /dev/kmem, read for the load average (the avenrun symbol); the SIOCGIFSTATS ioctl on a socket for interface counters; getsockname; svc_register and svc_run for the RPC service.
usr/etc/rpc.rstatd.role: Remote statistics RPC server. It reports the machine's load average and interface counters to remote callers, reading kernel memory through /dev/kmem.
usr/etc/rpc.rstatd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.rstatd: '/dev/kmem' and 'avenrun: can't seek in kmem' and SIOCGIFSTATS strings, dynamic imports ioctl and svc_register. The installed copy is the 64-bit build; the 32-bit build under the MODE-32bit path is not read.
usr/etc/rpc.rstatd.limits: A second build of this command sits at the same install path under a mode suffix (32-bit). It is not classified here.

usr/etc/rpc.bootparamd.interfaces: /etc/bootparams; the boot-parameter RPC program (its whoami and getfile procedures) registered over UDP; ioctl; svc_run.
usr/etc/rpc.bootparamd.role: Boot parameter RPC server for diskless or network-booted clients. It answers the whoami and getfile requests from /etc/bootparams.
usr/etc/rpc.bootparamd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.bootparamd: /etc/bootparams string, the whoami and getfile procedure names, the UDP registration message

usr/etc/cfsadmin.interfaces: /etc/mtab; the cache label files (the label-file get and put routines); the CacheFS in-use, mounted-check and directory-lock routines; the cache directory, scanned for symbolic links.
usr/etc/cfsadmin.role: Administers CacheFS caches. It works on cache directories and their label files, checks whether a cache is in use or mounted, and removes stale symbolic links left in a cache.
usr/etc/cfsadmin.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/cfsadmin: usage line, CacheFS routine names, 'Symbolic link found and removed' strings, /etc/mtab string

usr/etc/rpc.espd.interfaces: RPC service registration (svc_register, svc_getreqset, svc_sendreply); a session database (sgm_open_ssdb and sgm_close_ssdb); a default configuration loaded at start (sgm_load_default_conf); a framed XDR protocol (xdr_sgmframe).
usr/etc/rpc.espd.role: An RPC server for a session protocol whose frames carry an HMAC over the frame, and whose sessions are kept in a database. The binary does not say what the sessions are for; the purpose is unknown.
usr/etc/rpc.espd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.espd: sgm_* routine names (sgm_calc_hmac_auth, sgm_check_frame_auth, sgm_open_ssdb, sgm_load_default_conf), xdr_sgmframe, dynamic imports svc_register and svc_sendreply

usr/cluster/bin/cmond.interfaces: /etc/config/cmond.options; /etc/pcp.conf; the cluster database /var/cluster/cdb/cdb.db; the Unix sockets /tmp/.cmond_cdb.uds and /tmp/.cmond_client.uds; /var/cluster/cmon/process_groups; cap_acquire and cap_surrender; mmap.
usr/cluster/bin/cmond.role: Cluster monitor daemon for the cluster file system. It serves the cluster database to local clients over Unix sockets and keeps process-group records under /var/cluster/cmon.
usr/cluster/bin/cmond.citation: 6.5.30 usr/cluster/bin/cmond: the four path strings above, dynamic imports cap_acquire, cap_surrender and mmap

usr/cluster/bin/crsd.interfaces: the cluster database through the crsd_cdb_* routines (open, renew, stale, notify); the IPC socket /var/cluster/ha/comm/crsd-ipc; socket and bind; /etc/pcp.conf; cap_acquire and cap_surrender.
usr/cluster/bin/crsd.role: Cluster control daemon. It follows cluster database changes, keeps lists of clients and of pending requests, and exchanges messages with its peers on other machines.
usr/cluster/bin/crsd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/cluster/bin/crsd: crsd_cdb_*, crsd_clnt_* and crsd_process_remote_msgs names, /var/cluster/ha/comm/crsd-ipc string, dynamic imports bind and socket

usr/cluster/bin/cms_status.interfaces: the cluster database /var/cluster/cdb/cdb.db (default, or -f); the cicdb_* routines in libhacms.so.
usr/cluster/bin/cms_status.role: Gets or sets whether the cluster membership service (CMS) is enabled for one machine in a cluster. Options: -c cluster, -m machine, -s status, -t timeout; the meaning of -l was not read.
usr/cluster/bin/cms_status.citation: 6.5.30 usr/cluster/bin/cms_status: usage text with the -c, -m, -s, -t and -f options, cicdb_hasvcs_machine_in_cluster_status_get and _set names, libhacms.so string

usr/sbin/xfs_repair.interfaces: open and ioctl on the device nodes; device paths formed from /hw/major/%d/minor/%d; scratch files three scratch files under /tmp with random suffixes, one each for the data, log and realtime sections.
usr/sbin/xfs_repair.role: XFS file system checker and repair program. The three scratch names suggest it keeps simulated copies for the data, log and realtime sections when it runs without writing.
usr/sbin/xfs_repair.citation: 6.5.30 usr/sbin/xfs_repair: /hw/major/%d/minor/%d and the three scratch-file name templates under /tmp, dynamic imports open and ioctl

usr/etc/rpc.rquotad.interfaces: /etc/mtab (the mounted file systems); svc_register and svc_run for the RPC quota service; the RPC control call.
usr/etc/rpc.rquotad.role: Remote quota RPC server. It answers quota queries from clients for the file systems that are mounted on this machine.
usr/etc/rpc.rquotad.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.rquotad: /etc/mtab string, dynamic imports svc_register, svc_run and the RPC control call

usr/etc/rpc.ypupdated.interfaces: the NIS map directory /var/yp; TCP and UDP service creation (cannot create tcp service, cannot create udp service messages); svc_register and svc_run; ioctl; /dev/tty.
usr/etc/rpc.ypupdated.role: Network Information Service update daemon. It accepts requests from clients to change NIS maps kept under /var/yp.
usr/etc/rpc.ypupdated.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.ypupdated: /var/yp string and 'cannot create tcp service' and 'cannot create udp service' strings, dynamic imports svc_register and ioctl

usr/etc/rpc.rexd.interfaces: the temporary directory a per-request temporary directory named from the template /var/tmp_rex/rexdXXXXXX; two temporary mount-table files in /etc with random suffixes; /etc/mtab; the login records /etc/utmp and /etc/wtmp; mount, with an 'RPC create error' message on a failed mount.
usr/etc/rpc.rexd.role: Remote execution RPC server. It runs commands that remote clients submit, in a temporary work directory, and mounts the file systems those commands need, recording the session in the login records.
usr/etc/rpc.rexd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.rexd: a per-request temporary directory named from the template /var/tmp_rex/rexdXXXXXX, two temporary mount-table files in /etc with random suffixes, /etc/utmp and /etc/wtmp strings, 'not responding: RPC create error' message

usr/etc/rpc.passwd.interfaces: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/shells; the lock file /etc/.pwd.lock; the NIS directory /var/yp, with /var/yp/ypmake; /dev/tty.
usr/etc/rpc.passwd.role: Remote password-change RPC server. It changes a user's password in the local password and shadow files under a lock. Its message 'cannot specify passwdpathname AND use -D' shows that -D cannot be combined with a password-file path. The NIS directory and its make script (/var/yp/ypmake) appear in its strings, so a NIS update path exists; its trigger was not read.
usr/etc/rpc.passwd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.passwd: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/shells, /etc/.pwd.lock and /var/yp/ypmake strings, and the -D message

usr/etc/rpc.rusersd.interfaces: the terminal device prefix /dev/ in its strings; the utmp calls, among them getutent; svc_register, svc_run and rpc_control.
usr/etc/rpc.rusersd.role: Remote logged-in users RPC server, named after the rusers service. Few strings are present; the method of reading the user list was not read.
usr/etc/rpc.rusersd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/etc/rpc.rusersd: /dev/ string, the service name in the file name, dynamic imports svc_register and svc_run

usr/cluster/bin/ha_cmsd.interfaces: the cluster database /var/cluster/cdb/cdb.db; heartbeats sent to peer nodes over a named network interface; the SRM notify list, read under a lock; reset requests passed to the crsd connection; the usage line [options].
usr/cluster/bin/ha_cmsd.role: Cluster membership daemon. It sends heartbeats to the other nodes on the cluster network, updates node status in the cluster database, and passes reset requests for a node to the control daemon crsd, reporting when that connection is down.
usr/cluster/bin/ha_cmsd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/cluster/bin/ha_cmsd: heartbeat, 'Reset request for node %s ... crsd connection is down' and 'SRM notify list' strings, /var/cluster/cdb/cdb.db string

usr/cluster/bin/cmon_ctrl.interfaces: the cluster monitor daemon cmond (control requests); the options -f, -r, -g process_group and -l level.
usr/cluster/bin/cmon_ctrl.role: Command-line control for the cluster monitor daemon. Its action argument names an operation on the monitor; -g picks a process group and -l sets a log level. The action names are not read, so the operations are not described.

usr/cluster/bin/ha_gcd.interfaces: /var/cluster/ha/gcs/incarnation, /var/cluster/ha/comm and /var/cluster/ha/tmp; open, ftruncate and mmap on the files it keeps.
usr/cluster/bin/ha_gcd.role: Group communication daemon for the cluster high-availability layer. It keeps an incarnation record and memory-mapped state files under /var/cluster/ha.
usr/cluster/bin/ha_gcd.citation: 6.5.30 usr/cluster/bin/ha_gcd: /var/cluster/ha/gcs/incarnation, /var/cluster/ha/comm and /var/cluster/ha/tmp strings, 'mmap() of file' and 'ftruncate() of file' messages
